leftEvidence.title: The lawless one comes with Satan’s working, signs, and lying wonders

points.label: How power is described
points.left: The lawless one’s coming is “according to the working of Satan,” with power, signs, and lying wonders.
points.right: The dragon gives the beast his power, throne, and great authority.

points.label: Deception and allegiance
points.left: The scene includes Jesus’ coming, gathering, and deception. It also includes rebellion, restraint, and lawlessness. It also includes breath, appearance, and Satan’s working. It also includes signs, lying wonders, and truth. It also includes judgment. Together, these details meet in the passage.
points.right: A beast rises from the sea with crowns, hostile names, and a healed wound. The dragon gives it power, a throne, and authority. Worship, blasphemy, war against the saints, the earth’s people, and the book of life follow. The scene closes with captivity, the sword, endurance, and faith.

payload.posture: Read both WEBU passages side by side. Keep each passage’s actors, setting, order, and identity claims distinct.

rightEvidence.title: The dragon gives authority to a beast that draws worship and makes war

payload.tension: The lawless one comes according to Satan’s working. The dragon gives the beast power, a throne, and authority.
